content:
The image shows a cluster of green banana fruits with dark brown to black necrotic tissue rotting at the distal (blossom) tips of each finger. The rot is dry and shriveled, forming a characteristic appearance at the fruit ends — resembling the ash end of a cigar.

Key observations:
- Affected part: banana fruit tips (distal ends)
- Color: dark brown to black necrotic tissue
- Texture: dry, shriveled rot
- Pattern: confined to the tip of each finger, not spreading across the fruit surface
- No leaf involvement, no vascular symptoms

This matches **Cigar End Rot** perfectly — a fungal disease that causes dry rot at the tip of banana fingers, giving them the appearance of a burnt cigar end. None of the other classes fit: Panama Disease affects vascular tissue and leaves; Sigatoka/Cordana/Bunchy Top all affect leaves; Anthracnose typically causes sunken lesions with colored spore masses on the fruit surface.
